newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai soymeal steady to lower, corn prices ease.
newsitem.headline: Thai soymeal steady to lower, corn prices ease.

text.p: Thai soymeal prices were steady to lower this week as more animal feed ingredients arrived, trade sources said on Tuesday.
Corn prices were also pushed down on increased local supply, they said.
The feed industry, buoyed by reports that the European Union would open all its 15 markets to Thai frozen poultry exports from December 1, seemed reluctant to place new orders for the moment.
Currently, Thailand can only export frozen poultry to five EU members -- Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, Spain and the United Kingdom, according to a commerce ministry official.
Despite some tightness in soybean supplies, feed producers said they were comfortable with the current position as more feed ingredients had arrived or were scheduled to arrive.
Soymeal was quoted at around 10.20 baht ($0.408) a kg from 10.20-10.30 baht a kg a week earlier.
"We are well-covered for the year. But we might buy more if we receive any sign or assurance that the new tariff scheme will be effective by November 1 as scheduled," one feed producer said.
The cabinet earlier this month removed the import quota on raw materials for animal feed and cut import tariffs on soybean, soymeal and corn effective on November 1.
Government sources said on Tuesday that the new tariff scheme was likely to be on schedule.
One trader said he expected more buying orders if prices of soymeal, especially for meal of Indian-origin, dropped further.

"The prices have eased so far but many believe it could be lower,' he said. U.S. soymeal was being quoted at $310 per tonne c&f Bangkok, while Indian soymeal was being quoted at around $290 per tonne on the same basis, he added.

At least 90,000 tonnes of imported feed ingredients such as soymeal, wheat and corn gluten meal have arrived in Thailand since the beginning of October. An additional 7,867 tonnes of groundnut meal, sunflower meal and soymeal from India is scheduled to arrive on Thursday.
Next month, nearly 145,000 tonnes of soymeal and soy pellets are expected to arrive at Thai ports.

The vessel Northern Light is scheduled to arrive with 25,193 tonnes of Argentine low-protein soymeal on November 8. The Kavo Kaliakra is on the way from Brazil with 53,789 tonnes of soy pellets, expected to arrive on November 11.
The Vega T will arrive around November 23 with 20,000 tonnes of Brazil-origin soymeal and The Toscana is expected to arrive on November 25 with similar product from Argentina.

Corn prices dipped to 4.35-4.38 baht a kg from 4.40 baht a kg last week. Traders said the prices eased as more corn entered the market after floods began to subside. Floods have ravaged many parts of Thailand since the monsoon season started in late May. ($1 = 25 baht)
